captions.text: ReleaseGuard runs a real local experiment: a router, a stable service, a fresh baseline, and a candidate. All traffic is synthetic.
Policy is frozen before traffic starts. The first stage sends 5% to each comparison arm, with 90% going to the stable service.
Healthy is earned: every cohort needs enough evidence, a healthy baseline, and an upper degradation bound within tolerance. Advancement is explicit.
Stopping is checked against the real router. Subsequent requests must return the baseline version before withdrawal is recorded as confirmed.
Now lose the candidate telemetry. Missing measurements must not become zero errors or zero latency.
The run is inconclusive. Advancement stays locked, and candidate traffic is withdrawn after the frozen grace period. This is not a statistical regression claim.
Export includes the policy, raw requests, judgments, and control events. Reanalyze the saved inputs to reproduce the same decision.
